correctness.rationale: For each \(0<\lambda<1\), put \(a=1-\lambda^2>0\). The normalized Fock monomial basis and Tonelli give the exact nonnegative Hilbert--Schmidt trace integral \(\pi^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R^2}|g_\gamma(x+iy)|^2e^{-2ay^2}\,dx\,dy\). Fourier Plancherel of \(\mathbf1_{(0,1)}t^{\gamma-1}e^{-yt}\) gives the exact integral for \(\gamma>1/2\); converse Plancherel uniqueness proves divergence for \(0<\gamma\le1/2\). Completing the Gaussian square yields the exact factor \(\sqrt{2\pi/a}\). Every positive-cutoff Fourier integral defines a Hilbert--Schmidt operator for every \(\gamma>0\). A weighted-embedding change of variables bounds the operator-norm cutoff error by \(\varepsilon^\gamma e^{\varepsilon^2/(4a)}/(\lambda\gamma)\), proving compactness of all limits. A direct Riemann--Lebesgue argument independently verifies decay of the compactness profile. The Abelian integral limit proves the exact critical residue; a quadratic Taylor remainder gives logarithmic and power cutoff divergence. The actual bundled checker passed finite Fourier-Plancherel quadratures and numerical residue checks; numerical tests are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The result directly answers Question 7.1 in Barik--Sen--Paul (2026) negatively, already within the canonical classical Fock specialization. The explicit Fourier-endpoint family separates compactness from Hilbert--Schmidt membership, exhibiting the sharp \(\gamma=1/2\) threshold and a nonzero critical residue. It also provides quantitative compact approximation despite divergence of quadratic spectral energy. This is a substantive operator-ideal boundary beyond routine compactness and pure-composition estimates; no general Schatten-class characterization is claimed.
